skill_entry.name: A comment, log label or doc clause must match the code line it describes
skill_entry.trigger: Any one of these on an added line of the diff, in h/ or src/ (*.md hunks only for steps 7 and 8). (a) A comment that names a snake_case or backticked identifier inside a claim about code (captured from, comes from, set by, is set, sets, reads, waits on, waits for, already set, uses, performs, divides). (b) A comment with an angle-bracket placeholder (`<bdf>`), a path with a slash and an extension, a Q-notation token (`Q.61`), a negated parenthetical (`(no shuffle)`), or a trailing `?`. (c) A log or format call whose format string carries a label beside its argument list. (d) A hunk of at most 40 removed lines that replaces `type old = expr` with `type new = expr2` while a string or comment in the same block keeps the old stem. (e) A trailing comment whose first token is the declared name.
skill_entry.procedure: Map each line to HEAD through the `@@` headers; drop lines that also appear as removed lines after whitespace normalization (moved text). Identifier: confirm the token exists at HEAD; find the first assignment, wait loop or call of the sentence's subject in the next 90 lines (a header comment describes the body, not the signature); list that statement's identifiers. Token absent and a same-stem or same-struct sibling present is a finding, compared by name even when both hold one value. Label: pair each label with its argument, resolving a local alias one assignment back; grep the block L-20..L+40 for a stem the hunk re-derived; sort format strings for duplicates fed different objects. Placeholder: compare with the formatter argument in src/; grep h/ for the copy source. Path: resolve at HEAD, under h/, in an `#include` line or the PR file list. Tense, question, notation, negation: see the commands.
skill_entry.question: Does every identifier, placeholder, path, label, tense and negation in this sentence match the code line it describes, read at HEAD, and does a first-time reader get exactly one meaning from it?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A token that matches no symbol at HEAD (typo item). A token present in the described statement, or read only inside a callee (`hold_if_evictable` reading use_count, PR 2875). A trailing comment on a name no rename in this PR made self-describing, or one that disagrees with its own declared name (identifier-name-states-role). A default, plural or `or` subject (claim-wider-than-code). An include-form or resolving path (`runtron/stream_generate.hpp`, PR 2875); a non-resolving path in a *.md body (doc/pos_heap_v2.md:689, PR 2713 approved). A question-form one-liner above a constant whose name answers it (h/pos/config.hpp, PR 1707 approved). A stem surviving in another file. Moved text. Doc structure, kernel arithmetic, benchmark text, .py/.json/.yaml/CMake, comment-only PRs (3799, 4551 approved with no text). Never block: PR 2915 was approved in the same minute as the Q3.61 nit.
skill_entry.finding_shape: `<comment or label text>` (<file>:<line>) says <X>, but the line it describes (:<N>) uses `<Y>`, so a reader of the comment looks for the wrong thing. you mean `<Y>`? ```suggestion <corrected line> ``` ... right? per line <N> below. Or: fix the code so the comment is true, when the comment states the intent. When the hunk does not show the old derivation a label depends on: `Insufficient data: old derivation not in the hunk`.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit to minor, stated by form rather than by a word: a suggestion block with the corrected line plus `... right?` (3405930260, 3437533506, 3120684367), or a one-line question (`you mean 'hw_prepare'?`, `why are you calling this `HW O` if you're printing the Ra value?`, `would this read better if it said ...?`, `I think technically this should be `Q3.61` right?`, `probably won't exist for anybody else but you ;p?`). The one `normal` row (2771718489) is a debug label that misreports the quantity under comparison; it is still a question, and he approved the PR 22 minutes 39 seconds later at c502e4d61a. He flags one instance per stem and approves (worker.cpp:1070 `prep_done` and alloc.hpp:226 `<bdf>` were left unflagged).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk, then the full file at HEAD (the statement below the comment, the block L-20..L+40 for surviving old stems, the alias one assignment back), then other files (the formatter in src/ that produces a quoted string, the declaring header where sibling identifiers live, the sibling comment the text was copied from, `git cat-file -e` for paths), and for two rows hardware knowledge the hunk must show (the removed `/ *hw_sume` line: O = Ra / SUME; the stated integer-bit count: Q3.61). Not the PR body, commits, CI or a runtime run.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 14: a comment, log label or doc clause must match the code line it describes

Setup addition (for a merged PR, or when `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself): take the merge commit of the PR, `git -C WT log --first-parent --format='%h %p %s' origin/main | grep -m1 '#N'`, its first parent P (same as `gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha`), and set BASE = `git -C WT merge-base HEAD P`. On PR 3008 at HEAD c68ea87f48: merge aabd416676, P = 8811bdd35f, BASE = dd5dd82caf, pr.diff 1233 lines (merge-base with origin/main gave HEAD and an empty diff).

1. Harvest. `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src > pr0.diff; grep -n -E '^\+\+\+|^@@|^\+\s*(//|/\*|\*)|^\+.*(spdlog::|_log\(|fmt::format\(|TRACE_EVENT\()' pr0.diff > step1.txt` and `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- '*.md' | grep -n -E '^\+\+\+|^@@|^\+[^+]' > step1-md.txt` (prose lines carry no comment prefix; steps 7 and 8 read them, step 5 does not). Map each `+` line to HEAD file:line through the `@@` headers (a 12-line python over the headers). Drop a `+` line that also appears as a `-` line in pr0.diff after whitespace normalization (moved text; Wade reads it as unchanged). Record three counts: harvested, moved, new. Tokens per line: `grep -oE '\b[a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)+\b|`[^`]+`|<[a-z_]+>|\b[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.[a-z]+\b|Q\.?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?|\((no|without) [a-z_ ]+\)'`, run on the `+` lines only, never on the `+++` header.

2. Identifier check. Pre-filter: `grep -E '^\+\s*(//|\*).*\b(captured from|comes from|set by|is set|sets|reads|waits? (on|for)|already set|uses|performs|divides)\b' step1-new.txt | grep -E '\b[a-z][a-z0-9]*_[a-z0-9_]+\b|`[^`]+`'` (no bare `calls` or `returns`: they hit prose such as 'invariants between calls' and 'Always returns true'). For each token: `git -C WT grep -q -w TOKEN HEAD -- h src || echo "NO SYMBOL: typo item"`. Described statement: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'L,L+90p' | grep -n -E '\bSUBJECT\b *=|\bSUBJECT\.(load|store|wait)|\bSUBJECT\('` and take the first hit (a header comment describes the body, not the signature: on PR 3008 the comment is :1112, the signature :1118-1129, the assignment :1138). List the identifiers of that statement with the token regex of step 1. Token absent: siblings by stem `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'L,L+90p' | grep -oE '\b[a-z]+STEM\b' | sort | uniq -c` and by struct `git -C WT grep -n -E 'TOKEN|SIBLING' HEAD -- <declaring header>`. A callee that reads the token internally is not a sibling. Compare by identifier, never by value: both `wres_fields.fields.hbm_cnt` and `ares_fields.fields.hbm_cnt` are set from `hbm_count` at :656-657, and the row is still a finding.

3. Label check. 3a pairs: for each added format call `grep -n -A3 -E '_log\("|spdlog::|fmt::format\("' full/FILE`; read the label before each `{}` against the argument in that position; resolve a local alias one assignment back (`sed -n 'L-15,Lp' full/FILE | grep -n 'ARG *='`; `prepare_tail {}` fed `dbg_wqe_idx` matches because :1725 reads `dbg_wqe_idx = dev->prepare_tail`). Only an argument whose source statement names a different quantity is a finding. 3b renamed quantity, bounded: keep hunks with at most 40 removed lines (`@@ -a,r +b,s @@`, r <= 40); inside one such hunk pair `^-\s*(float|double|auto|int|uint64_t|size_t) [a-z_]+ =` with `^\+\s*(float|double|auto|int|uint64_t|size_t) [a-z_]+ =`; keep the pair when the new name differs and the expression differs beyond the rename (a dropped `/ *hw_sume`). Then `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'L-20,L+40p' | grep -n -E 'OLDSTEM'` in strings and comments; list every survivor inside one finding per stem. A stem that survives in another file is not this check. When the hunk does not show the old derivation and the label needs hardware meaning (O = Ra / SUME), write `Insufficient data: old derivation not in the hunk`. A refactor hunk above 40 removed lines goes through 3a only. 3c duplicates: `grep -oE '^\+.*_log\("[^"]*"' pr0.diff | sed 's/^+ *//' | sort | uniq -d`; read the argument lists; identical arguments are not a finding.

4. Placeholder check. `grep -n -E '^\+.*(//|\*).*<[a-z_]+>' pr0.diff`; take the literal prefix and `git -C WT grep -n -F 'PREFIX' HEAD -- src`; compare placeholder i with argument i of the `fmt::format`. Copy source: `git -C WT grep -n -F '<bdf>' HEAD -- h` (replace the placeholder). Member test: `git -C WT show HEAD:<declaring header> | grep -n -w bdf`.

5. Path check, comments in h/ and src/ only: for every path token from step 1 run `git -C WT cat-file -e HEAD:PATH 2>/dev/null || git -C WT cat-file -e HEAD:h/PATH 2>/dev/null || git -C WT grep -q -F "\"PATH\"" HEAD -- h src t || grep -q -E "(^|/)PATH$" prfiles.txt || echo "MISSING PATH"`.

6. Tense. For each present-tense mechanism sentence naming function F: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- FILE | grep -n -E '^-.*(recurs|F\()'` and `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk '/F\(/{p=1} p' | sed -n '1,200p' | grep -c -E 'recurs|F\('`. Removed by the diff and 0 at HEAD: the sentence must be past tense.

7. Open questions. `grep -n -E '^\+\s*(//|\*).*\?\s*$|^\+.*(originally thought|proposed change|TODO: decide|should we)' step1.txt step1-md.txt`. Fire only when the question is about a mechanism or a decision AND the same PR either implements the answer in the statements below (fields, waits, branches: dma_xfer_state end_desc/readback fields) or removes a sibling comment that posed the same question (`git -C WT diff BASE HEAD | grep -n -E '^-.*(Proposed change|originally)'`, PR 2011 driver.cpp). A one-line question above a constant whose name answers it (`// How many metadata entries does the device hold?` above `metadata_entry_count`) is house style, not a finding.

8. Notation and wording. `grep -oE 'Q\.?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?' <comment block>` versus the integer-bit count stated in the same block and `git -C WT grep -n -E '_q[0-9]+\b' HEAD -- FILE`. Negation: for `(no X)` or `without X`, `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk '/F\(/{p=1} p' | grep -c -i X`; 0 hits = the sentence states an absence (`(no failure path on this leg)` with no false return) and is not a finding; hits where X is done to the input before the call = precondition, propose `pre-X`. Docs: `grep -n -E '\([A-Za-z0-9 ]+ (excepted|accepted|aside|excluded|included)\)' step1-md.txt`, write both full-sentence readings. Trailing restatement: `grep -n -P '^\+\s*[A-Za-z_:<>, ]*\b([a-z_]+);\s*//\s*\1\b' pr0.diff` (Perl mode; `grep -E` with `\1` fails on ugrep).

9. One finding per line, siblings of the same stem listed inside it: the comment or label, the deciding code line, a suggestion block with the corrected line, `... right?`. Both repairs named.

On PR 3008 (HEAD 17c6e0117d, comment commit c68ea87f48, BASE dd5dd82caf): step 1 = 133 added comment and log lines, 63 moved, 70 new, all in src/pos/worker.cpp; step 2 pre-filter hits c68ea87f48:src/pos/worker.cpp:1112 "hbm_cnt is captured from ares_fields before any WLR mutation" (tokens ares_fields, hbm_cnt); the described statement is :1138 `hbm_cnt = wres_fields.fields.hbm_cnt;`; ares_fields is absent from it and the sibling wres_fields is present (12 uses versus 9 in :1112-1200; both out-params of prepare_cmd_words at :563-564). Finding = 3437533506; applied at 17c6e0117d:1112 "wres_fields". Other pre-filter hits (:1130, :1153, :1217, :1235, :1348, :1373, :1476-1478, :1502) pass the identifier test or carry no identifier. Step 3a: 18 added log lines, 0 findings after the alias rule (:1727, :1746). On PR 2980 (comment commit 247c8a4c22): step 4 hits h/pos/device.hpp:663 `<bdf>`; the formatter src/pos/device.cpp:625 and :630 passes dev->idx; `bdf` is not a PosDevice member (only `int idx` at :255); copy source h/pos/alloc.hpp:226 `<bdf>` whose formatter src/pos/alloc.cpp:366 and :371 also passes dev->idx. Finding = 3405930260; applied at a62d15a3dc:device.hpp:663 `<idx>`; alloc.hpp:226 still `<bdf>`. On the silent set (15 PRs probed): PR 1707 h/pos/config.hpp:51 no longer fires (step 7 narrowed) and PR 2875 token_tree.hpp:324 `runtron/stream_generate.hpp` resolves under h/ (step 5); 0 findings on the rest.
final.widen_delta: New check, no existing check widened. Boundaries with existing checks: check 5 keeps TEST_CASE and SECTION names versus their assertions; this check takes labels in production log strings and comments in h/ and src/. Check 9 keeps machine-local paths and log names inside PR-body Status/Verification/Tests/Results sections; this check takes a path named in a code comment in h/ or src/, never in a *.md body. Check 6 keeps compile-time guarantee sentences and (as widened by claim-wider-than-code) any sentence whose subject is a default, a plural, an `or` or an `every`; this check takes identifier-by-identifier agreement between one sentence and the statement below it. Boundaries with sibling new items: the typo item keeps misspellings and identifier-shaped tokens that match no symbol at HEAD (LOG_TOKEN_TIMS, 3125494616); this check takes a token that exists as a symbol but is not the one the described statement uses (ares_fields). Orchestrator note: rename the typo item from 'Misspelling, run-together words, wrong identifier or over-wide line ...' to '... identifier that matches no symbol ...' so two items do not claim one trigger. identifier-name-states-role keeps a trailing comment that disagrees with its own declared name (tok_ix_per_b, 3075717295); this check compares a comment with the statement below it. The SKILL.md front-matter description gains one clause: "comments, log labels and doc clauses that disagree with the line they describe". The Setup section gains the merged-PR BASE rule (merge commit's first parent), which every check needs when run on a merged PR.

Step 2: replaced 'next non-comment lines up to the blank-line block' with 'first assignment, wait loop or call of the subject in the next 90 lines; a header comment describes the body'; kept the strict sibling rule (absent AND same-stem or same-struct sibling present; a callee reading the token is not a sibling); added compare-by-identifier-not-value (:656-657 both set from hbm_count); stem count corrected from 8 to 9 ares_fields in :1112-1200 (measured).
